This idea resonates with the philosophical notion that some aspects of reality are ineffable, meaning they cannot be fully described or understood through language. This idea aligns with linguistic relativity (also known as the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis), which posits that the structure of a language affects its speakers' cognition and worldview.
